title: What Should a Monthly Digital Marketing Report Include?
description: Build a useful monthly digital marketing report that separates completed work, channel activity, spend, qualified enquiries and the next decision.
summary: Follow a fictional Varanasi catering business as it replaces a dashboard full of activity with a short report the owner can question and act on.
body:
What should a monthly digital marketing report include? Start with the business decision, not a collection of screenshots. A useful report names the agreed work, records channel activity using each platform's definitions, shows provider fees and media spend separately, checks received and qualified enquiries with the business, explains important changes and ends with the next action and owner.

The report should not combine search impressions, ad clicks, social reactions, AI citations and qualified enquiries into one success score. Those signals answer different questions. The reader should be able to trace every conclusion back to an owned account, a defined enquiry record or a documented delivery item.

Anita receives many charts but cannot approve the next month

Imagine Anita runs a fictional catering service in Varanasi. The business, owner and situation are original planning examples, not a SiteSutra client story or reported result. Her provider sends a long monthly dashboard showing website visits, search impressions, ad clicks and social engagement.

The report does not say which landing page changed, how much of the payment went to advertising, whether form submissions reached the inbox or which requests matched the catering service. A green arrow appears beside several numbers, but nobody has recorded what should happen next.

Anita does not ask for more charts. She restructures the report around a chain of evidence: agreed work, channel activity, delivered enquiry, qualified conversation and next decision.

Use five sections that the owner can verify

Anita's hypothetical monthly reporting structure
SectionQuestion answeredEvidenceOwner check
Work completedWhat was changed, published, tested or reviewed?Named pages, campaigns, assets and completion datesWas this in the agreed scope?
Channel activityWhat did each platform record?Account source, date range and metric definitionCan the business access the source?
Commercial inputsWhat did the work and distribution cost?Provider fee, media spend and subscriptions kept separateDoes spend match the approved arrangement?
Enquiry qualityWhich real requests reached the business and fit the service?Private enquiry register reviewed by the response ownerWere suitable requests handled?
Next decisionWhat will continue, change, stop or be tested?Reason, owner, dependency and review dateIs approval required before action?

A small report can cover these sections. Page count is not evidence of care, and a live dashboard is not a substitute for interpretation.

Report delivery before claiming an outcome

Anita's provider begins with the agreed scope. The report lists the service page revised, the campaign destination tested, the search query review completed and the form delivery check performed. Each item has a date and a link or account location the owner can inspect.

This prevents recurring activity from becoming invisible. It also prevents an outcome claim from replacing the delivery record. A change may be completed correctly without yet producing enough evidence for a performance conclusion.

Keep each channel's metric definitions intact

Google Search Console defines impressions, clicks, click through rate and average position within Google Search reporting rules. Average position is an aggregate, not the permanent rank of every page. Anita therefore reviews page and query trends for a complete date range rather than treating one property average as a business result.

Google Ads defines clicks as interactions with an ad and cost as spend for billable interactions. A configured conversion action is still a platform event. If the conversion is a phone link click or form action, Anita checks separately whether the call connected or the form reached the monitored destination.

Social platform activity and email activity remain in their own sections when those channels are actually in scope. The report does not add unlike actions together merely to create a larger total.

Separate management, production and media spend

Anita's report has separate lines for the provider's management work, one time website or creative work, advertising paid to the platform and recurring tools. This mirrors the commercial agreement and makes the next budget decision possible.

The report does not invent an attribution model or claim revenue that the business cannot connect to a real record. If a catering enquiry later becomes a booking, the private sales record can note the source evidence and limitations. Customer details do not belong in the public report or website repository.

Match the report to the current working arrangement

Open the statement closest to the business. These prompts decide what evidence deserves attention; they do not create universal targets.

The business has no CRM or formal sales system

Use a simple private enquiry register with received date, route, requested service, suitability, response and next step. Agree who maintains it. Do not pretend platform clicks are sales because a later outcome cannot yet be joined reliably.

Paid advertising is active

Show media spend separately from fees, name the campaign and destination, include the platform's activity and conversion definitions, and reconcile configured actions with received enquiries. Record budget changes only after approval.

SEO and content are the main work

List technical or content delivery, then review Search Console pages, queries, impressions and clicks across comparable complete periods. Keep indexing, visibility and qualified enquiries as separate stages.

AI visibility is being sampled

Keep a dated prompt set, assistant or platform, response and cited public source. Do not combine those samples with Search Console visibility or claim that a mention is a recommendation, ranking or enquiry.

Compare periods only when the comparison is fair

A monthly boundary is convenient for billing and review, but it does not make every comparison meaningful. Anita notes campaign dates, website releases, service changes, holidays and incomplete data before interpreting movement.

Search Console warns that newest data can be preliminary and that aggregation changes between property and page views. The report names the selected filters and date range, and it does not hide a small sample behind a percentage.

If the evidence is too sparse for a conclusion, the report says so. “Continue collecting comparable data” is a valid next decision when nothing specific supports a change.

End with an action register, not a celebration

Anita's final section contains four possible decisions: continue an agreed activity, change a defined element, stop an unsupported activity or run a bounded test. Every row names the evidence, owner, dependency and next review date.

A decision can also sit with the business. The owner may need to approve a service statement, respond to missed enquiries, provide accurate photographs or confirm campaign capacity. A provider report should make those dependencies visible rather than blaming the channel.

Build the report from inspectable evidence

Download the monthly digital marketing report template (CSV). Replace the examples with the agreed work, source account, period, metric definition, observation, limitation, decision, owner and review date.

Keep customer names, phone numbers, private sales values, passwords and exported account data outside this public template. Share sensitive reporting only through an approved private process.

Ask what changed and what decision follows

Anita's shorter report does not make every chart disappear. It gives each chart a job. She can see what the provider delivered, what each platform recorded, which real enquiries reached the business and what must be approved next. No metric is promoted into a result it cannot prove.
